audit_items.proof_trace: The function reads the last attendance record (L43-44) then inserts the toggled type (L49-50) in plain READ COMMITTED isolation with no row-level lock (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), no advisory lock, and no `SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE`. Two concurrent calls on the same `p_card_id` will both observe the same `v_last_type` and both insert the same `v_new_type`, corrupting the attendance state (e.g., two consecutive `'out'` records). The `SECURITY DEFINER` declaration and the single-function structure provide no serialization guarantee.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An attacker (or concurrent NFC read) sends two simultaneous HTTP POST requests to the Supabase RPC endpoint (`/rest/v1/rpc/record_attendance_by_card`) with the same `p_card_id` using the public `anon` key; both transactions read the same last type, compute the same toggle, and commit duplicate attendance records — causing a phantom clock-in or clock-out that falsifies the attendance log.
